Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". input.description: Find highest fan-in function in internal/
input.prompt:
This is a Go repository at /bench/repo. I need to find which single function or method declared under the internal/ directory (77 .go files there) has the highest inbound-call count (fan-in) — i.e., is called from the most call sites across the entire repository (not just internal/, but the whole repo including cmd/, and any other top-level dirs).

Steps to do this:
1. List all function/method declarations in internal/**/*.go (grep for `^func `).
2. For each candidate function/method name, grep across the whole repo (excluding the declaration line itself, excluding _test.go if you want but you can include tests too) for call sites — e.g. `\bFuncName\(` or `pkgname.FuncName(` or `receiver.MethodName(`.
3. Focus especially on small utility-like packages (internal/util, internal/base, internal/storage, internal/filter, internal/httpgetter, internal/idp, etc.) since those tend to have widely-used helpers. Common candidates: logging helpers, error wrapping helpers, config getters, context helpers, string/slice utils.
4. Count approximate call sites for the top 10-15 candidates and report the single winner with the highest count.

Be careful to distinguish: a method name that's very common (like `Get`, `Close`, `String`) will have false positives from unrelated types — try to disambiguate by checking that call sites actually correspond to the internal/ package's type/import, or at least sanity check a sample of call sites.

Report back: the winning symbol name, its file path (relative to repo root), and an approximate fan-in count (number of call sites), plus the runner-up for comparison. Keep the report under 300 words.
